MLK × I-285 — the interchange TEST (exit 9)▾

A test scene, same treatment as the crest, Tatum and overpass ones — real ground, real individual trees, look-test roads — framed on the third crossing type: an interchange, where Martin Luther King Jr Dr passes OVER I-285 on a bridge and ramps climb between the two levels. The focus is the one you set: the rise — I-285 sits low, MLK rides high, and the ground itself climbs from one to the other under the ramps. Test scene only, not game data.

The ground (read this first — it is not the package): this crossing sits about 390 m east of the terrain-test package's edge, so the scene's ground was built from the same USGS 3DEP tile, by the same method — not taken from the package. What it measures: I-285 runs in a cut here, its surface at 862 ft under the bridge, while MLK's line stands on the ridge at 889–897 ft — the natural ground differs by about 34 ft across the crossing. That difference is the whole scene.

The bridge: MLK crosses on a deck 80 m (262 ft) long at 886 ft, girders under the slab, open air beneath — clearance 17 ft (5.1 m) over the freeway. Different from Fairburn: there the road simply crosses. Here there are two levels, and earth that climbs between them.

The ramps — one pair drawn, the pair you named: the off-ramp leaves I-285 low (862 ft), loops south-east and climbs on a rising embankment — up to about 1 ft of built-up ground under it — to meet MLK at the top. The on-ramp leaves MLK at the high level and falls away down its own embankment (up to about 4 ft) to merge into I-285. No floating ribbons: every ramp sits on sloped earth. The interchange's other ramps exist in the ground (their mounds are in the measured terrain) but are not paved in this scene — the pair is the point.

One honest conflict, flagged for the roads step: the redraw record for this deck (AN-11) settled MLK's level at 878 ft, worked out as freeway-surface-plus-clearance. But MLK's own measured approach ground reads 889–897 ft on both sides, and the ramps' recorded profiles tie into MLK up at that level — a deck at 878 ft would dip below both its approaches. So the scene builds the deck to the measured ground (886 ft), the way every structure in this programme is built. The record gets corrected at the roads step, not silently here.

The trees are real trees — 2266 of them, placed one by one, foliage starting about 8 ft up, same as the other scenes. One declaration: the measured tree-canopy clip ends just west of this window, so east of its edge the cover is extended from its nearest measured column. The trees are set dressing in every scene; the ground is the measured article.

What to check: from the side (the profile view), the two levels and the ramp embankment climbing between them should read at a glance. From the off-ramp driver's view, you climb the fill toward MLK the whole way — the ground rises with the road, and nothing floats.
